description:
[narrowed from grading-credits-the-selected-arm-not-the-model-that-served-after-failover] OBSERVED 2026-09-12, and it affects the drafting-grade mechanism landed today. The grading captures model_selection.selected from the resolver response, which names the arm the bandit CHOSE. When that provider fails the resolver FAILS OVER to another model and serves the completion from it, so the work is done by a model that is not the one being graded. EVIDENCE: over three hours the resolver logged 'provider exhausted for anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 - falling back to google/gemini-2.5-flash' repeatedly, plus NINE anthropic 401 authentication errors and THIRTEEN anthropic cooldowns. Yet claude-haiku-4-5 now carries a feature_compose posterior with one observation and an expected value of 0.333, while google/gemini-2.5-flash sits at 0.125 over six. Since haiku appears never to have actually served a drafting completion in that window, its posterior is most likely built from work gemini performed, and gemini's own penalties are correspondingly understated. WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS THE ONE JUST FIXED, one layer down: today's attribution work made sure the graded arm is the one that served the PLAN call rather than the last completion of a compose. This is the same question asked of the provider layer - the graded arm must be the model that actually produced the text, not the one selection nominated. A bandit that credits an unreachable arm for a reachable arm's output will keep choosing the unreachable arm, which is exactly the behaviour visible here: haiku is repeatedly selected and repeatedly falls back. NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and worth one cheap check before any fix: whether the resolver REWRITES model_selection.selected after a failover. If it does, the concern collapses and the posteriors are already correct; if it does not, the grading is mis-attributed whenever failover occurs, which the logs show is frequent. REQUIRED CONTRACT: the response must report the model that SERVED the completion, distinctly from the model that was selected, and grading must use the served model. CLOSURE CHECK: force a completion whose selected provider is unreachable, then assert the arm credited is the one that served it and not the one nominated. CONFIRMED BY READING THE CODE, 2026-09-12 - this is no longer a hypothesis. Two facts settle it. First, model_selection is assigned once from the selection metadata: '(result as Record<string, unknown>).model_selection = sel.meta;' and a fleet-wide search finds NO reassignment of sel.meta.selected anywhere, so the reported selection always names the arm the bandit nominated. Second, the failover helper walkFallbackModels serves the completion from a DIFFERENT client and returns '{ ...fb, fallback_from: fromModel }'. So on any failover the text is produced by one model while model_selection.selected still names another, and grading built on that field credits the wrong arm. THE REMEDY IS EASY BECAUSE THE SIGNAL ALREADY EXISTS: the response carries fallback_from precisely when a failover occurred. A consumer can therefore either skip grading when fallback_from is present - conservative, loses a few observations, never mis-attributes - or better, have the resolver report the SERVING model explicitly alongside the selected one and grade the server. The second is preferable because failover is frequent here: nine anthropic 401 authentication errors and thirteen cooldowns in three hours, with claude-haiku repeatedly nominated and repeatedly falling back to google/gemini-2.5-flash. CONSEQUENCE FOR TODAY'S NUMBERS, stated so nobody over-reads them: claude-haiku-4-5 shows a feature_compose expected value of 0.333 on one observation despite apparently never serving a drafting completion in the window, while gemini sits at 0.125 on six. Some of gemini's penalties are probably recorded against haiku. The mechanism is sound and worth keeping; the arm labels on the first dozen observations should not be trusted until the serving model is reported.

WHY PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS ON THIS GAP FAILED (most recent last):
- wrong_location: adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 0.90, 0.90): The patch adds 'served_model' to the response in both failover and non-failover paths (lines 1110 and 1289), but there's no evidence the GRADING syst
- wrong_location: The patch changes the grading handler to accept 'graded' rather than 'model', but does not ensure grading is based on the served model rather than the nominated one.

Do not repeat these failures. Address the specific cause named above. The specification is above; this failure text is context only and is not the specification.]
